content:
elaine: Sharing the draft PRD for the Optimize recommendations feature. TL;DR: guidance engine + config UI that suggests batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles per workload. looking for short feedback on launch gates and must-have acceptance criteria. https://redwood.internal/prd/optimize-recs-draft :eyes:

matt: skimmed. seems solid. couple quick asks: how do we validate correctness of quantized model outputs vs baseline? need a regression threshold and test harness.

elaine: agree. initial idea: run eval suite on a heldout prompt set (customer and synthetic), require <=1% regression in exact-match/semantic-score for critical prompts, and per-customer opt-out. thoughts?

sunita: +1 on eval suite. also add stability by seed; quantization can nondeterministically change outputs. require <0.5% variance in embedding cosine for embed workloads.

kai: ops perspective: rollout plan must include fallback to non-quantized variant and capacity detection. propose canary=5% traffic for 24h with p50/p95/p99 latency checks and cost delta monitoring.

ryan: customers care about cost savings and not quality loss. recommend including a customer-facing SLA note: if quality drops >1% on customer-specific eval set, auto-rollback and credit.

elaine: good. draft launch gates so far: (1) automated eval pass (<=1% QA regression, embeddings <=0.5% cosine drift), (2) latency SLO met for 95% within target, (3) cost improvement >=10% vs baseline for the workload profile, (4) rollback path + canary, (5) docs + samples. ok?

matt: add acceptance criteria for batching: must support per-route dynamic batch sizing and not increase tail latency >5ms for interactive routes. we should have a synthetic test that exercises short-seq traffic.

sunita: edge cases: (a) mixed-type requests (chat + embedding) in same route — ensure isolation of caching buckets, (b) KV cache eviction races on scale-down, (c) quantized FP16->INT8 fallbacks when accuracy drops. specify behavior for each.

elaine: noted. drafting specific acceptance lines now. sample config snippet in PRD so reviewers see intent:

```
optimize_profile:
  route: "/chat"
  batching:
    mode: dynamic
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
    latency_target_ms: 120
  caching:
    kv_prefix: "session"
    ttl_seconds: 300
  quantization:
    allowed_modes: ["int8", "fp16"]
    quality_guard: 0.01  # fractional tolerated regression
```

kai: ops nit: include telemetry keys we need: model.variant, quant_mode, batch_size, cache_hit, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost_per_1k_tokens. also an event for auto-rollback with reason code.

matt: tests: add a chaos test that kills one GPU during canary to validate fallback works and no request loss. infra-bot can we schedule a job?

infra-bot: scheduled: canary-chaos-test on 2026-04-04T03:00:00Z for 2h. job id: cj-8492.

ryan: prioritization note: customers A, B, C asked for offline quant recommendations first. propose shipping embeddings recommendations (lower risk) in phase 1, then chat generation in phase 2.

elaine: I like phased approach. Phase 1 (embeddings): offline recommender, batch tuning, embed stability checks. Phase 2 (generative): online canary, batching heuristics, quantization. Phase gating required between phases.

sunita: acceptance checklist additions for embeddings: 99% of customer queries must have embedding cosine drift <=0.5 over baseline and embedding latencies within 1.2x baseline.

matt: final ask: include a small migration guide for customers who pin model ids; ensure we can offer model-variant mapping table and temporary compatibility layer.

elaine: perfect. I'll update PRD with these gates + items and tag folks for a quick RFC review tomorrow. action items: @matt write short test plan snippets, @kai list telemetry + rollback codes, @sunita produce eval prompt sets for top 3 customers, @ryan confirm customer rollout priorities. aim: RFC sign-off by EOD Friday. :calendar: 

kai: acknowledged.

matt: on it.

sunita: will start building eval sets.

ryan: I'll sync with CSMs and get list.

elaine: thanks all. leaving open for comments — ping me for any hot takes. :sparkles:
